title: Challenging the Evaluator: LLM Sycophancy Under User Rebuttal

live_model.evidence: Table 9: "gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14 OpenAI"; Table 4 row "GPT-4.1-nano 74.6* 66.1* 66.5* 56.1* 80.3 73.6" (F, Fc, Fi for FR vs Judge).

prompt.location: Appendix D (MCQ question prompt template), D.1 (Full/Truncated/Answer-only rebuttal templates), Table 3 (examples)
prompt.note: Two-turn conversation: original answer, then a rebuttal carrying a disagreeing answer from another LLM.

claim.metric: persuasion percentage F under Full Rebuttal (FR)
claim.location: Table 4 / Table 5, row GPT-4.1-nano, column F (FR); average 118.8 disagreement pairs per dataset over 5 MCQ datasets (Table 2)

data.source: Public MCQ datasets (Table 1); the fixed disagreement pairs (challenger answers sampled from other LLMs) are not linked to a release

notes: Soft gap: the disagreement pairs depend on gpt-4.1-nano's own first-turn answers and on randomly selected challenger responses from seven other models, so an exact re-creation is impossible; the protocol is fully described. Decoding temperature is not stated.

resolution.plan: Re-create the protocol from Sec. 3: sample 300 questions per dataset (CommonsenseQA, LogiQA, MedMCQA, MMLU, MMLU-Pro) with a fixed seed; obtain gpt-4.1-nano-2025-04-14 zero-shot CoT first-turn answers with the Appendix D template; build disagreement pairs with challenger answers from still-callable models of the Table 9 pool (challengers drawn from correct responders whenever the target is wrong, aiming at the ~50:50 split of Table 2); send the Full Rebuttal (D.1 template) as the second turn and measure the persuasion percentage F; compare with 74.6 (Table 4).
resolution.approximation: The original fixed pairs (randomly selected challenger responses) cannot be recovered, so the pair set and challenger pool differ; temperature is not stated.
